name: Mecasermin rinfabate
lead: Mecasermin rinfabate (brand name Iplex, also called rhIGF-I/rhIGFBP-3) is a complex of recombinant human insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) bound to recombinant IGF binding protein 3, given by daily subcutaneous injection. It was developed by Insmed to prolong the half-life of IGF-1 and potentially reduce side effects such as hypoglycemia [3][11].

Its original target was growth failure in children with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency or growth hormone insensitivity [4][11]. According to Wikipedia, the product was withdrawn from the market for short-stature indications following a patent settlement, and research moved to other conditions [11].

Clinical work in the sources covers myotonic dystrophy, Duchenne muscular dystrophy, retinopathy of prematurity and other conditions [12][13][14]. It is discussed in this wiki because of interest in height and bone growth; the sources contain no data on use for height in people with normal IGF-1 and no looksmaxxing forum discussion.

paras: Growth hormone acts at the growth plate directly and through IGF-1, and a large share of the hormone circulates bound to binding proteins [4]. Binding IGF-1 to IGFBP-3 was intended to prolong its circulation and reduce adverse effects relative to IGF-1 alone (mecasermin) [3]. Drug reviews describe its pharmacokinetics, safety profile and efficacy [3][5][6].

The initial indication was growth failure from severe primary IGF-1 deficiency, including children with growth hormone gene deletion who developed neutralizing antibodies [4][11]. Wikipedia reports a phase II study in myotonic muscular dystrophy that found increased muscle weight but no improvement in grip strength or walking tests, with lab changes including higher testosterone and LDL and lower triglycerides and HDL [11]. Registered studies include phase 1/2 trials in myotonic dystrophy (NCT00233519) [12] and Duchenne muscular dystrophy (NCT01207908) [13], and phase 2 trials of IGF-1/IGFBP-3 for prevention of complications of prematurity such as retinopathy of prematurity (NCT01096784, NCT03253263) [14][15].
Wikipedia states that the complex was reported to have fewer side effects, such as hypoglycemia, than mecasermin alone [11]. A fuller safety profile is described in drug reviews [3][6].

Human studies have examined growth disorders, myotonic dystrophy, Duchenne muscular dystrophy and prematurity-related conditions [3][11][12][13][14][15]. No studies of mecasermin rinfabate for height gain or bone length in people with normal growth were found.

card.summary: An IGF-1/IGFBP-3 injectable built for rare growth failure; no data supports height gain in people with normal growth.
card.note: Withdrawn for short-stature indications; no data for normal-height use.

quick.overview:
Mecasermin rinfabate (Iplex) pairs recombinant IGF-1 with its binding protein and is injected under the skin. Insmed developed it for children with severe IGF-1 deficiency.

It was withdrawn for short-stature indications after a patent settlement, and trials moved to muscular dystrophy and prematurity conditions. No studies address height in people with normal growth.
quick.mechanism: Binding IGF-1 to IGFBP-3 was designed to extend how long IGF-1 stays in circulation and to reduce side effects such as low blood sugar.
quick.risks: Reported effects in trials included lab changes such as higher testosterone and LDL in myotonic dystrophy patients. It is a prescription biologic, and published safety data come from patient populations.
